next_step: Closed-lost declared; schedule re-engage in 12 months if budget/security posture shifts
notes: Background: VaultGrid provides hardened ICS control software for water + energy utilities. Strong regulatory requirements — cannot rely on vendor-managed control plane.
Primary ask: fully air-gapped deployment (no egress) + on-prem management, HSM-backed key storage, 5y retention controls.
Engagement arc: started Jan 2025 as high-priority inbound RFP, AE + SE introduced POC proposal for private bundle (3x A100 equiv.).
Security review: SSO + SOC2 not sufficient for them; required FIPS/HSM and no external control plane. Legal insisted on on-prem only and source access for critical components.

POC: ran initial on-site eval plan in Feb — SE validated offline containerization and model artifacts, but architecture still required vendor code review + signed attestation (not feasible in hosted/dedicated).

Decision: Procurement team communicated 2025-03-01 — vendor must be deployable in fully air-gapped environment with vendor-provided support but zero outbound connectivity. Redwood proposal required minor outbound telemetry for autoscaling and fallback; legal rejected.

Competing offers: they shortlisted LocalOps Inference (on-prem appliance) and an internal team building stripped-down transformer runtime. LocalOps committed to firmware-level appliance with signed audits. VaultGrid selected LocalOps.
Budget: mid-year budget freeze announced; procurement put multi-vendor buy on hold but LocalOps offered capital purchase + support contract that fit current CAPEX window.

Customer quote from procurement lead (paraphrase): 'We can't accept any external control-plane traffic — our regulators would not sign off. If you can deliver a fully air-gapped appliance with signed binary attestations, let's revisit.'
AE notes: stalled after decision; no internal champion identified (previous champion moved to another program). Follow-up plan: quarterly check-ins + invite to Redwood Private product updates.
timeline: 2025-01-10: Lead created from inbound RFP (water-utility category)
2025-01-15: Intro call (AE Jordan Meyers) — discussed architecture requirements; SE intro scheduled
2025-01-22: SE deep-dive (Priya Nair) — reviewed on-prem container options, identified telemetry constraint
2025-02-27: Red team/legal review requested signed attestation for binaries — flagged as blocker
2025-03-01: Procurement decision communicated — selected competitor; declared closed-lost
reason_lost: Strict air-gapped / on-prem appliance requirement + no internal champion + budget timing; competitor offered appliance model that met regulatory attestation needs
